dashboard_recap.headline: MLB Daily Recap - July 11, 2026
dashboard_recap.article:
**Pirates Pull Off Upset Sweep in Thrilling Series Against Brewers**

In a stunning series, the Pittsburgh Pirates upended the Milwaukee Brewers in a two-game sweep, with Esmerlyn Valdez emerging as the top performer. The 23-year-old slugger hit two home runs, including a grand slam, and drove in six runs in the Pirates' 6-7 win on the first day. He added another home run and two RBIs in the second game, a 2-3 Pirates victory.

On the pitching side, Braxton Ashcraft was the standout, allowing just one hit and no runs in six innings of work in the first game. In the second game, Bubba Chandler and Shane Drohan combined for 9.2 innings of shutout relief, with Chandler striking out six in 4.2 frames.

**Royce Lewis Leads Twins Past Angels**

In the American League, the Minnesota Twins took down the Los Angeles Angels 5-3, with Royce Lewis delivering a strong performance. The 22-year-old shortstop went 2-for-4 with a home run and two RBIs, helping to power the Twins' offense.

On the mound, Joe Ryan pitched six strong innings, allowing two runs on six hits with six strikeouts. Tommy Nance earned the win in relief, striking out three in 1.2 innings.

**Goldschmidt and Grisham Lead Yankees Past Nationals**

In the National League, the New York Yankees edged the Washington Nationals 4-2, thanks in part to a strong performance from Paul Goldschmidt. The first baseman hit his 15th home run of the season, a solo shot in the seventh inning.

Trent Grisham also had a big day for the Yankees, going 2-for-4 with a home run and two RBIs. Cam Schlittler pitched 6.2 innings of relief, striking out six and allowing two runs on four hits.

**White Sox Shut Out Athletics**

In a one-run game, the Chicago White Sox took down the Oakland Athletics 1-0, thanks to a strong performance from Gage Jump. The 24-year-old right-hander pitched 5.2 innings, allowing one run on five hits with seven strikeouts.

Chase Meidroth had a big day at the plate for the Athletics, going 2-for-3 with a double and one RBI.

**Giants Beat Rockies in Nail-Biter**

In the National League, the San Francisco Giants edged the Colorado Rockies 4-2, thanks in part to a strong performance from Casey Schmitt. The 23-year-old catcher hit his fifth home run of the season, a three-run shot in the second inning.

Kyle Freeland pitched six strong innings for the Rockies, allowing four runs on six hits with nine strikeouts.
